A quick pick on the page is recorded as his yes and never as a ruling. Most of what was called decided is PROVISIONAL and names what it waits on. source: docs/design/overhaul/decisions/all.json (one row a call), docs/design/overhaul/review/00-critical-review.md and F-framework-audit.md, and docs/design/overhaul/00-the-game.md (the front of the book)
vision: You run four heroes from your first day. They hunt while you are away, and you win by preparing them: who stands where, what they wear, what their bars do and where you send them. Every choice is made once and remembered. Harder tiers hit harder and pay more, and the four you send is your call. Gear is a chase with rare finds. Levels never end, and gear, sinks and old grounds keep pace by formula. Around the hunt stands a shared world that works while everyone sleeps: clans, world bosses, events and two arenas, paying buffs and gear. Crowns buy Premium, looks and comfort, and trade to other players for gold. That gold is a real edge, as far as the player market holds what it buys, and a player who never pays can reach the same things with gold. Every number comes from formulas you can read.

ruled.what: All four heroes from the start. No slot prices. (GR-2)
One Premium for each account.
No solo or group balance targets. Party buffs make hunting together the obvious choice. (GR-67)
The four together, on the tier they can hold, earn more for each hero than the same four split up. A lone hero is a slower choice, never a trap.
The MMO layer is clans, world bosses, events and PvP arenas, and it is heavy work going forward.
Decisions first. No build lanes until every decision is made and a build plan exists.
Buying Crowns and selling them for gold gives real advantages, just not broken ones.
The MMO layer rewards buffs and gear, because that is what drives players to buy Crowns and sell them for gold.
Two PvP arenas: one with normalized stats and one that uses your gear.
The current game is irrelevant. Nothing is compared with it. Its data is evidence only.
Balance is fixed at the formula layer. No ground, weapon or monster gets its own patch or its own math.
Nothing planned for later is cut. It is built later and stays hidden until it works.
The itemization plan is a source of record.
Every time number assumes a player hunts 12 hours a day, measured in low, mid and best gear, to Level 400.
The Level table is the clock of a mid-geared four on the hardest tier it holds.
Level 400 takes 4,580 hunted hours, which is day 382.
Best gear is about 15% faster and takes about 15% less damage than mid gear.
A death costs 6% of all Level XP, flat, with no cap.
The harder tiers kill at a flat count at every Level. A mid-geared party on Deadly dies 50 to 100 times in 1,000 hours.
The weekly limits on chest opens stay.
120 days of grounds at Early Access, and each region opens 30 days before the first fours arrive.
The Luck bar keeps its hours: +16% at 500 hours, +39% at 5,000.
A player may cost at most $0.15 an account a month at 1,000 accounts, and no more at 10,000.
Bought gold has no limit on how much sooner. The limit is on what can be bought.
Two visits a day is the free game.
Heroes work in town for all 12 rested hours.
A full set of the best gear takes about one band to Krell, then one to two regions.
Crafting is a quarter to a half of the step from mid gear to best gear, and a player who never crafts can buy it.
The too strong and too weak thresholds stand, and any cut goes to you on one list first.
One Global chat, with lines sent in small batches and a slow mode when crowded.
Clan castle goods keep their prices. Only the two goods that cannot be made are fixed.
A unique can be reforged up a band and keeps its property. Each new band also gets uniques of its own.
The every-idle-hour training reading is a number we watch, never a gate.
Faction skills are sized to matter.
Spells are sized first, then Deadly.
Storm and Bone runes unlock at Runecrafting 25 and 40.
Cleave merges into Turning Cut.
Rend stays at 6 seconds and the axes do not hold Power Strike.
Mend heals about 11% of max health.
The hammer has its own strike that spends an Earth rune.
The crossbow has its own spell list. Sixteen Necrotic and Storm spells in all.
Only people are weak to Necrotic.
Every spell is sized at Level 10 and at Level 60, so heals and first strikes land whole in the first hours.
Krell is weeks away, not months: day 18 for a four.
The recommended option of every call in the four dives of 11-20 is approved.
Tempering carries up a tier and costs only the difference.
Generous drops through Krell, really rare and strong after.
Luck has two feeds and no more: rivets used and Bestiary stages.
The harder tiers hit harder, sized on a party with a healer and monsters that shoot the back row.

rederivedByFable.what: The lot-size clause no longer leans on a gold target. A lot is a fixed count of Crowns. Thirty days of Premium costs a whole number of the smallest lot, so a gold buyer never holds a stranded remainder. The book opens with no seeded gold price and the first asks set it.

The cap wording changes and the cap stays. It is a weekly count of Crowns an account may sell and buy on the book, as ruling 24-5 requires. It opens as a fixed count of Crowns from a data row. Once the book has seven days of sales the server re-derives the count each week from the players' own 7 day median price, aimed at about one account-week of hunting gold. It reads the price players made and never sets one. It is a clamp against laundering and floods. It is not a ceiling on how far ahead bought gear can put a hero.

The 1.65 reading does not move, because it is the caps and the ruled best-gear state. The paying-alone reading stays about 1.22 against a plain mid-geared four in the same band, and it now says what it is: the pace of a four in the best gear state with the +6% boost. It is reached only when the market holds the pieces, and it is not a limit on gear. If a set bought on the market ever reads over the ruled 15% above mid gear, the fix is at the formula layer (the best-gear definition or the gear curve), never a cap on buying.

Clamp 2, the price band, reads the players' own 7 day median. Before a median exists it has no seeded target price: the band is a wide floor and ceiling from a data row whose only job is to stop one Crown being used as a gold transfer.

designerRulings.note: Ruled by the game designer on 2026-11-21 and reported to Tyler. They are not new decision rows. D-9, the Talents curve, is not ruled yet. D-12 to D-23 are named in 14-the-rest.md for the next ruling file.

rulings.ruling: The Path is one table of 21 row families, each reading its Level from its own system's file. The wand card says casting costs gold, about 100 on the first hunt. In the first hour the coach rings only screen controls. A harder tier is offered with no Level and no ground: when the party's last hunt there read Safe and the tier's risk row, at the gear the party wears, is inside the ruled death band.

A standing plan line, "Wear upgrades", puts better gear on at every Start and every hunt end, in town. Nothing changes inside a running hunt. The leader is the hero the engine sends in front, and the player may pin another. "Needs you" holds eight kinds in a fixed order, one row a kind, three shown.

The armor curve is x2.4, or x1.6 if the confirm run shows it holds the same steps. The arrival kit is the mid kit one band back, in gear only. An arrival is graded by survival, pace and the tier it can hold, and S5.low is a report. Tiers 1 to 7 keep their built armor. Carter's Rest, the Ox Road and factions stay staged. A heavy piece pays for armor with lighter blows. The kill reward under Level 5 follows the curve at exponent 1.1.

The Blessing ladder's threshold is 5 hunted hours of the pace seat, Tyler's own number of S-5, now with a reason under S-12 a. Rungs halve what is left, and their Levels come from the law: about 97, 140 and 257.

Refills, Blessings, the talent reset, rename and colors are rows of hours at the hero's Level. The first refill of a day is 2 hours of wage. Deeds are set once in account-days, and rooms and chests move by one factor. `wageShare` opens at 0.80. The Weighhouse stays the first project as a building only, and the market trades from day one.

The sample world boss is Mossback, an old brook bear, fought at the Mill Pond in each party's own room on the one monster formula. The chest pays by the account's own points at 2, 6 and 12 Normal party-hours: a buff, one Mossback Cloak, then the buff's second week. Both names are new and are not in the game's data yet.

A 28 day cycle with two beats in the first build: the Hearthrise on weekend 1 and the world boss on weekend 3. Weekends 2 and 4 stay quiet. The fire lights at +10% Level XP and gains +3% a mark to +25% at five marks. A full fire is a quarter of the fuel the week's active accounts find. The weekly Open Halls row is retired.
On call opens at hero Level 10, once the account has a friend or a clan. The default tier limit is Dangerous. `onCallXpShare` stays 0.10.

Party-wide damage stays in the data, the `group` rows of the monster spells, and gets no tier row in the first build. Hask's Ford and the Muster Barrows each gain one group caster. A tier row is a named fallback with a measured trigger.
A rest plan's usual ending is a standing job with no count. It starts no hunt, never loops and stops by itself after 24 hours. "Wait in town" stays a choice. No rest plan ending starts a hunt.
